title: Slope 2 is derived from Slope 1 and alpha so the rate curve lands exactly on the Borrow Maximum Rate at 100% utilization
content:
A.4.4.1.3.5.1.1.4 defines `Slope 1` as "the spread of the SKY Borrow Rate over the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate when Utilization is at Target Utilization," and A.4.4.1.3.5.1.1.5 defines `Slope 2` as "the spread of the SKY Borrow Rate at 100% Utilization over the SKY Borrow Rate at Target Utilization." A.4.4.1.3.5.1.1.5.3 then supplies a methodology rather than a free choice: "Under normal circumstances governance should set the `Slope 2` parameter based on the following formula: `Slope 2 = Slope 1 * alpha`," where alpha (A.4.4.1.3.2.1.5.3) is `((SKY Borrow Maximum Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) / Slope 1) - 1`.

Substituting shows what the rule enforces: `Slope1 + Slope2 = MaxRate − MinRate`. In other words, the two segments must together span exactly the distance from the floor to the ceiling, so the curve reaches the SKY Borrow Maximum Rate precisely at 100% utilization — no earlier (which would flatten the top and remove the scarcity signal) and no later (which would leave the stated maximum unreachable and meaningless).

This reduces the real degrees of freedom. Governance chooses the floor, the ceiling, the target, and Slope 1; Slope 2 follows. Fewer independent parameters means fewer ways for a well-intentioned adjustment to produce an inconsistent curve, and it makes the Borrow Maximum Rate a genuine boundary rather than an aspiration.

The hedge — "under normal circumstances" — leaves room to break the identity deliberately, but doing so should be recognized as changing where the curve tops out, not merely as tuning its steepness.
description: With alpha = ((MaxRate − MinRate)/Slope1) − 1 and Slope 2 = Slope 1 × alpha, the steep branch is a consequence of the endpoints rather than an independently chosen parameter.
